pageCache.text:
Small Haven School - Independent Special Needs School
Our school motto is ‘Belong, Believe, Thrive, Achieve.’
Stacey White
Principal Head
“Welcome to our Small Haven School website. We provide pupils, whose varying needs could not be met in other education placements, with a chance to have a sense of belonging within a school community where they can thrive.”
The children are at the heart of everything we do and each individual is valued and respected as an important member of the school community. ‘Every child matters.’
Small Haven School is passionate about the holistic development of the child and understands that unless children have their social and emotional needs met they are unable to learn. The school offers a safe and caring therapeutic learning environment facilitated by positive and trusting relationships, containing boundaries, and positive reinforcement. This calm and nurturing environment helps our pupils develop the confidence to take risks and discover their skills and aspirations. An open and reflective culture is encouraged for both staff and pupils in order to learn from experience and grow together.
I feel privileged to lead such a wonderful and ‘Outstanding’ school and feel immensely proud of the efforts and achievements of the pupils, parents, and dedicated staff who make it so special.
We hope you enjoy exploring the website and gain a greater insight into our diverse school community. If you are still left with questions, please do not hesitate to contact us. You are also very welcome to arrange a visit and experience first hand what makes Small Haven so unique.
We work in partnership with parents, carers and children and pride ourselves on our good communication with them and with other associated organisations and professionals. The work of the school is underpinned by an ethos of positive expectations and mutual respect.
About Small Haven
The school promotes the development of essential knowledge and skills in order to meet the everyday challenges of life in the twenty-first century.
Our broad and balanced differentiated curriculum is designed to be exciting, challenging and engaging so that children are curious and want to learn. School should be a fun and meaningful childhood experience with an opportunity to discover one’s possibilities, make lasting friendships and create memories to treasure. We are committed to supporting our pupils in developing learning habits that extend beyond the school boundaries so that they become life-long learners.

Upper School
We have one class in Upper School at Small Haven – Keller.
Keller Class
“Optimism is the faith that leads to achievement. Nothing can be done without hope and confidence”.
Keller Class is located within the Upper School at Small Haven. Named after the inspirational Helen Keller, who overcame significant sensory challenges to succeed in her learning and development, this class promotes a ‘can do’ attitude to both academic and social challenges.
We actively use the Growth Mindset philosophy to think more positively about areas we may find difficult in our learning and are supportive and caring towards one another. We like to have fun and work together to create fun and interesting learning experiences that we can all enjoy.
Keller class teacher is Mrs Tolfree supported by our TA Sam.

Home-School Meetings
Small Haven School recognises that parents and carers are a crucial part of our school community.
Your views and support are invaluable to the successful running of the school. Small Haven’s ‘home-school’ meetings give parents and carers the chance to stay informed about the school’s development, student council meetings, upcoming events and other news.
Meetings also enable parents and carers to offer their feedback and suggestions, which are paramount in Small Haven meeting children’s needs and the school’s development. In addition to this, the meetings provide an informal opportunity for parents to get acquainted with one another.
Small Haven School welcomes all parents and carers to join these meetings in Term 2, Term 4 and Term 6. These take place in the meeting room located in the office building, where there will be hot beverages and biscuits provided!
We thank you in advance for your ongoing support and look forward to working with you.
Wednesday 19th November 2025 – 9am
Wednesday 4th March 2026 – 2.30pm*
Wednesday 17th June 2026 – 9am
*Please note the later time to accommodate parents who can’t make morning meetings.

pageCache.pageTitle: Lower School - Small Haven School - Independent Special Needs School - Kent
pageCache.text:
Lower School
We have two classes in Lower School at Small Haven – Disney and Christou.
Disney Class
“All our dreams can come true if we have the courage to pursue them”.
Welcome to lower school Disney class! Named after the inspirational Walt Disney. Our aim is to spark a love of learning in the children and to learn through inquiry and discovery, and further explore their creative abilities and imagination.
Our teachers are Miss King and our TA is Sophie and we have a small group of up to 4 children in our class. We aim to give the children the best start on their Small Haven School journey, equipping them with the confidence and skills they will need to succeed, not only in school but in their everyday life.
In our class this year we are going to focus on:
Settling into school life
Building our reading and writing skills
Improving our spelling
Practising key maths skills
Working towards our individual targets
Handling our emotions
Developing a positive mindset
Making friends and having fun!
Christou Class
“Don’t judge a book by its cover, it’s what’s on the inside that counts…”
Named after Nikki Christou, winner of ‘Child of Courage Award 2016,’ we are a class that celebrates diversity and promotes courage in overcoming challenges.
As the upper class in lower school, we continue to develop a love of learning through fun and engaging lessons whilst also preparing pupils for secondary education. Children are encouraged to discover their skills and interests and we shine a light on their achievements to promote a positive self-image as learners and individuals.
Essential learning and skills are further embedded and developed through a multi-sensory approach alongside a comprehensive social and emotional development curriculum.
Our teacher is Miss Titmarsh and our TA is Tim.

pageCache.text:
Middle School
We have two classes in Middle School at Small Haven – Attenborough and Nightingale.
Attenborough Class
“The only thing we have to fear is fear itself…”
Attenborough Class is named after the inspirational Sir David Attenborough. There are lots of reasons why Sir David is such an inspiration to us, but one of the main reasons is that Sir David has done more than almost any other person to help millions of us understand and appreciate the wonders of the world around us.
Attenborough Class is a small class taught by Mrs Holden and supported by TA’s Sally & Kim .
As a class, we chose the following 7 values that our class is built on: Determination, Creativity, Kindness, Openness, Adventure, Compassion & Fun.
Nightingale Class
“I attribute my success to this, I never gave or took any excuse”.
Florence Nightingale is known for great things. Her compassion, her commitment and her diligence to her work are what makes her such an icon, and allows our class to follow in her footsteps.
Nightingale Class is one of the middle school classes at Small Haven and we aim to grow caring and nurturing individuals, who are each set on achieving their own personal goals. We are a creative group, who will show our learning, our ideas and express ourselves in our own individual way.
We are building friendships, whilst learning both in and outside of the classroom, ensuring to have fun, whilst learning about the world around us.
Nightingale class is taught by Miss Verrill and supported by our TA’s Ki & Natasha.

Sixth Form
We have one main class and a break away class in the Sixth Form at Small Haven this year.
Our Vision
The aim of our sixth form is to empower each and every learner to thrive, grow and achieve their fullest potential in an inclusive and supportive community.
In our sixth form we are committed to nurturing confidence, independence, and essential life skills, empowering students to embrace their next steps – be it further education, meaningful employment, or active participation in their community – with resilience and self-belief!
ACE Pathways
In Small Haven School’s Sixth Form, we offer three tailored pathways – Achieve, Connect, and Employ (ACE) – to meet the unique needs and aspirations of our learners. These pathways are designed to empower students to develop their independence, prepare for further education, or take their first steps into the world of work.
The Achieve Pathway
The Achieve Pathway focuses on helping learners build and enhance their independent life skills, ensuring they are ready to thrive in their everyday lives and future aspirations. This pathway is carefully tailored to meet individual needs and goals, encompassing:
Achieve is perfect for students who are looking to grow their confidence and self-reliance in a supportive and structured environment.
The Connect Pathway
The Connect Pathway is designed for learners planning to transition into further education in the next year. This pathway equips students with the tools, confidence, and guidance they need to take their next steps. Key features include:
Connect ensures students are well-prepared for their educational journey ahead, fostering confidence and readiness for this exciting new chapter.
The Employ Pathway
The Employ Pathway supports students in preparing for and stepping into their chosen career paths. With a focus on real-world experience and job readiness, this pathway offers:
Employ is ideal for students with a clear focus on entering the workforce, providing them with the experience and confidence they need to achieve their ambitions.
Each pathway at ACE is designed to support our learners as they transition toward greater independence, education, or employment, ensuring they are equipped to succeed in their unique journeys.
Opportunities for All Learners at Small Haven School Sixth Form Provision
Irrespective of the pathway, – Achieve, Connect, or Employ – every learner has access to a broad range of opportunities and learning experiences that foster personal growth, practical skills, and community engagement. These include:
In Sixth Form we are committed to delivering a holistic education that equips learners for their future, whether their path leads to increased independence, further education, or employment. Alongside academic and vocational development, we prioritise personal growth and fostering a strong sense of community connection.
Our unique and specialised sixth form is housed in a self-contained, two-story building, as well as having an additional classroom adjacent to the main school office. The provision is supported by Mr Gwyther – Deputy Head, Collette – Occupational Therapist and Mrs Oliver the school SENCO. The class teacher is Mr Mole and the teaching assistants are Kyle and Amy. Additionally, specialist staff deliver and support specific subjects throughout the week, ensuring a tailored and comprehensive learning experience.
The building features a large classroom, a fully equipped kitchen, a digital media room, and a spacious common room, creating a dynamic environment for learning, creativity, and social interaction. While our sixth form operates independently of the main school, we value opportunities for our students to remain integrated into the wider SHS community.
To foster responsibility and community spirit, sixth form pupils take on meaningful roles within the school, such as assisting with catering for events, organizing fundraising activities, or supporting major school occasions like shows and sports days. This blend of independence and collaboration ensures that our learners develop vital skills while maintaining their connection to the SHS family.

pageCache.pageTitle: What people say - Small Haven School - Independent Special Needs School - Kent
pageCache.text:
What people say about Small Haven School
Don’t just take our word for it, here are a few quotes from the Ofsted Inspector, parents and pupils.
Quotes taken from the Ofsted Report dated 10th – 12th December 2024
“Pupils offer a warm and joyful welcome to their deeply caring and ambitious school. The motto of ‘Belong, Believe, Thrive, Achieve’ permeates all aspects of school life. Expectations are consistently high and impressively met. Pupils achieve well. They progress through the curriculum with success, while also developing interpersonal qualities and life skills. Behaviour is excellent. Staff provide pastoral support and encouragement to help pupils stay on track if they feel unsettled. Conduct around school is calm, focused and friendly. Relationships between pupils, and with staff, are delightful. Everyone communicates with respect and compassion, ensuring a supportive and purposeful learning atmosphere across every class. One pupil represented many when sharing, ‘This school welcomed me with open arms and always believes in me’.
“Personal development is exceptional. Pupils proudly present and record the school’s podcast using their cutting-edge studio. Music, sport and creative arts are celebrated and nurtured to find the best in everyone. Trips are extensive, enriching the curriculum for all. The school boosts pupils’ spiritual awareness with visits to places of worship such as a synagogue. Leadership roles enable pupils to make a tangible difference to school life. Opportunities include ‘head of online safety’, ‘friendship champion’ and ‘recycling monitor’. Pupils value these responsibilities enormously”.
“Behaviour is impressive. Expectations are widely understood, ensuring positive behaviour in and out of the classroom. Pupils socialise and play joyfully in their well-kept recreation areas. Staff are always nearby to help pupils navigate any challenges, such as agreeing the rules of a game. Everybody feels equal here. Pupils are sympathetic to the needs of others and are proud to help each other”.
“Reading is valued highly. All staff are trained to teach phonics and reading using the school’s programme. Pupils hear precise modelling of sounds and use consistent resources. Catch-up activities, individual support and group lessons utilise well matched texts, giving pupils the help they need. As they progress through the school, pupils become fluent, confident and motivated readers”.
“Excellent personal development opportunities help pupils to become conscientious citizens who want to improve the world. This is achieved through a raft of thoughtful initiatives including creating Christmas packages for homeless charities. Visitors enrich school life and help pupils to understand moral issues. For example, pupils welcomed a visit from a refugee who inspired them to understand the plight of someone fleeing war. Older pupils support younger pupils as buddies. The courteous and inspirational sixth-form students are role models for others. The student council makes a tangible difference to school life. Pupils write and present manifestos before everyone considers their vote. This is one of many examples of how fundamental British values are promoted successfully. Cookery is important across all ages, helping pupils to develop life skills. This is made possible by the proprietor’s strong investment in high-quality facilities which are accessible to all”.
“Parent and carers are unanimous in their high praise for leaders and the school. They say this is ‘an amazing school where children are fully supported to thrive’. The Inspection report: Small Haven School 10 to 12 December 2024 school provides extensive help for families and ensures that views of parents are well considered. Staff feel happy, proud and highly valued. Careful considerations about workload ensure positive well-being for all. Every decision is made with pupils at heart. The proprietor’s vision to provide life-changing learning for pupils with SEND is fulfilled every day with expertise, dedication and compassion”.
Quotes taken from Parents
"For any perspective parents/guardians contemplating this school as a potential placement for their child, the clue is very much in the name. It is indeed a Haven and a very safe, secure and friendly haven at that. They are of course a school and always endeavour to educate on all levels, including social and life skills, but their endeavours go so much deeper than that and all delivered in a very relaxed, cosy and understanding environment."
"Thank you we really do appreciate all your help and for never giving up on our son. You’re one in a million all of you."
"Meeting the children’s needs whilst stretching their potent is a true balancing act and Small Haven deliver this with such thought, empathy, planning and fore-sight that the Parent, Guardian or Child are often unaware of the fact that such a well-oiled caring machine is forever ticking over and striving at all times for perfection. Yes we are of course dealing with young people who are themselves dealing with a whole spectrum of challenges, and no system is perfect because we as people are not perfect, but this school is as close as you will ever find."
"Some great news, our girl has gone to college and we have not had a phone call. She was so nervous but she went in confidently and enjoyed it. It wouldn't be possible without all your hard work so thanks again."
"They are a true paradox, they strive to push their pupils to full fill their potential but at the same time there is an extremely relaxed atmosphere around the whole school. The staff are extremely professional but they are also very human and approachable as well. From top to bottom I have only ever seen staff that are friendly and committed."
"I’d like to thank you all for your continuing support with my son, he is thriving under your care and is happier than he has been for a very long time. This progress, in part is due to the school’s therapeutic approach which has enabled my son to grow emotionally and this has impacted positively on his self-esteem. The format of the school and the dedication of the staff team, should not be kept a secret, as what is taking place at Small Haven is worth shouting about. THANK YOU ALL! Just a brilliant review and yes when a child attends Small Haven they can dream big!"
Quotes taken from children
"Small Haven School is like my second home. We’re like one big happy family."
"The teachers make me feel safe at Small Haven School. Everyone says hello and is friendly."
"The adults look after me here and I have lots of friends. Every day I want to come to school, which I didn’t at my old school."
"My favourite thing about Small Haven School is I know they will listen to me."
"The work is challenging but I understand it and the staff help me. I can talk to the adults when I’m upset or angry."
"I feel safe here because it is a small school and the staff are helpful and nice. I have someone I can talk to if I need to."
"My favourite thing about school is my friends and teachers."
Quotes taken from Professionals
"All three students I supported who attended your school, had very different but very complex special educational needs. During their time at Small Haven School; each developed a positive view of themselves as learners, became more independent and confident in their learning and became more self-reflective about their behaviour/actions and how these impacts on others. The school's planning for transition to Post 16 was personable and considered, with each pupil receiving a bespoke package of preparation and support. Whilst leaving a very small school, for bigger pastures, each left with the confidence that they could go forth and succeed. I look forward to the pleasure of working with you in the future, should any of our students be so fortunate as to attend your school."
"As an external guest, regularly visiting your school for Personal Educational Plans (PEP) Meetings, I would like to commend you on the professionalism of your staff. The meetings were always well prepared for in terms of feedback on attainment and progress, as well as the emotional development of the pupil. This, combined with the detailed completion of the PEP Forms made the holistic educational needs of the student explicit to all involved."
"I have been extremely impressed by Small Haven. The welcome is always warm and professional from staff. First impressions are so important to students, parents and professionals alike and give a good indication of the care and professionalism of the provision. Your reports are of an excellent standard. They are detailed and very clear whilst your style of chairing meetings is relaxed and informative. You and your team’s understanding of and support to the children you care for is admirable. As a social worker I very much appreciate your support. Many thanks"
